title: Deadline day, and the punishment could be weeks away

segments.say: Today is the deadline for Manchester City to appeal the biggest verdict in Premier League history.
But the bigger story might be what comes after it.
Quick recap. On Tuesday, an independent commission found City broke Premier League rules on 114 of the 115 charges.
City deny any wrongdoing. They say they will appeal, and that the ruling contains clear errors.

visual.text: Clear material errors, of law, principle and fact

segments.say: The Times reports the commission will hold a separate hearing to decide City's sanction, and it could come within weeks, not months.

visual.sub: Not months, according to the report

segments.say: Under Premier League rules, the options include a fine, a points deduction, or other sporting sanctions.
For comparison, Everton lost 8 points in total, while Chelsea were fined £10.75m after reporting themselves.
So that's the road so far. Charged in February 2023, a hearing that started in September 2024, verdict on Tuesday, appeal deadline today, and a punishment still to come.
So what's fair? A big fine, or a points deduction? Tell me in the comments, and follow so you don't miss Day 5 tomorrow.
